counterfactual_missing_items: No documented family history of rickets or short stature consistent with XLH
FGF23 undetectable (in XLH typically elevated; suggests other cause)
Renal ultrasound shows medullary nephrocalcinosis more typical of phosphate wasting disorders other than classic XLH
decisive_items: inappropriately normal phosphate excretion for the degree of hypophosphatemia
severe left knee pain and bilateral genu valgum deformity
response.rationale: R3 is the only candidate and its raw spans cover hypophosphatemia, abnormal phosphate handling, and valgus deformity. However, key counterfactuals (undetectable FGF23, elevated 1,25(OH)2D, nephrocalcinosis) argue against classic X-linked hypophosphatemia and point toward an alternative diagnosis (e.g., renal phosphate wasting with elevated calcitriol).
